clue.text: Vessel has slate on lip

parts.note: lip and sauce both mean cheek or impudence
to slate a play is to criticise it harshly

explanation.surface: A pot is described as having a stone edge.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue 'slate on lip' puts the criticism word after the cheek word.
explanation.definitionFit: A saucepan is a cooking pot, a kind of kitchen container with a handle.

clue.text: Awkward son went off the straight and narrow

parts.words: went off the straight and narrow

explanation.surface: A clumsy boy strays into bad ways.
explanation.definitionFit: Stilted speech or writing is stiff and unnatural, lacking ease.

clue.text: A French ass, say, mostly loud and clear

indicators.note: mostly means not all, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: an ass is an example of the horse family

explanation.surface: A French donkey brays plainly.
explanation.definitionFit: Unequivocal means leaving no doubt, so a statement that is unambiguous and plain.

clue.text: Reader's issue with English agreed by school

explanation.surface: A pupil's problem with English is acknowledged by the school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reader's issue' sounds like a magazine number; it is a reader's tired eyes.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyestrain is fatigue of the eyes, a common complaint from long periods of reading.

clue.text: Unnatural profit, in a way, with vodka and beer?

indicators.note: the profit word goes within the letters for a way

parts.note: both drinks are made from cereal crops

explanation.surface: A drinks firm's odd way of making money.
explanation.definitionFit: Going against the grain means contrary to one's natural inclination.

clue.text: Settle down in Arsenal's opening match

indicators.note: an opening is where something begins, so only the first letter of the club name is kept

parts.note: the start of the club name
a match is a light for a cigarette

explanation.surface: Things calm down at the start of a football game at Arsenal's ground.
explanation.definitionFit: A bird or passenger that alights comes down and settles on a perch or the ground.

clue.text: No republican initially changing sides? He won't

indicators.note: the first letter swaps one side for the other, right for left

explanation.surface: Someone opposed to a republic insists he will never switch allegiance.
explanation.walkthrough: R (right) at the start changes to L (left). 'He won't' means he won't change sides.
explanation.definitionFit: A loyalist stays faithful to a cause or ruler, so by nature never defects.

clue.text: Blooming head of theatre and choir take off

indicators.note: off means gone bad, so the letters are spoiled into a new order

explanation.surface: The theatre director and choir are told to leave the stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head of theatre' looks like a director; head belongs to the definition, the flower head.
explanation.definitionFit: The globe artichoke is a thistle whose edible part is the large unopened flower bud.

clue.text: It helps musician to grin, with funk playing

indicators.note: playing about with letters moves them freely into a new order

explanation.surface: A musician smiles while playing funk music.
explanation.definitionFit: A tuning fork sounds a pure fixed pitch that players use to tune instruments.

clue.text: Calm down, please: official's inside

indicators.note: the letters sought sit inside the run of words just before it

parts.note: found across the end of the first word and start of the second

explanation.surface: Someone asks for calm because an official has arrived.
explanation.walkthrough: The colon and possessive are ignored; the letters run from pl-EASE across OFF-icial.
explanation.definitionFit: To ease off is to relax effort or let tension drop, which is to slacken or quieten.

clue.text: Entitle army corps to pull back holding detainee

indicators.note: holding means keeping inside, so the detainee goes within
pulling back means retreating, so the corps letters run upwards

explanation.surface: Army engineers retreat while guarding a prisoner.
explanation.definitionFit: To empower someone is to give them authority or a right, granting them a claim.

clue.text: Note what's up in the papers?

indicators.note: in a down entry up means reading from the bottom

parts.note: the fourth note of the sol-fa scale
eh is a way of saying what?, so eh's

explanation.surface: Someone asks what's happening in the newspapers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'What's up in the papers' sounds like asking for the news; papers are just a bundle of sheets.
explanation.definitionFit: A sheaf is a bundle, and a sheaf of papers is a bunch of documents held together.

clue.text: Frank, mostly sensible, is running

indicators.note: mostly means nearly all, so the last letter is cut

explanation.surface: A man named Frank is described as fairly sensible and out jogging.
explanation.walkthrough: Frank looks like a name, but is an adjective for candid.
explanation.definitionFit: A machine that is running is in working order and functioning.

clue.text: Pretty female making an impression

parts.note: an etching is made by cutting an impression into a plate

explanation.surface: An attractive woman makes a big impact.
explanation.definitionFit: Fetching means attractive or charming in appearance.

clue.text: Go crazy, in a spin

indicators.note: spinning round turns a word around, so these letters are read upwards

explanation.surface: Someone loses their head and panics.
explanation.definitionFit: Both nouns mean an attempt or try, interchangeable in idioms such as having one at a crossword.

clue.text: Modish poem contains a line on worker, perhaps without style

indicators.note: the poem word holds the following pieces within its own letters

parts.note: the worker ant, with perhaps marking an example

explanation.surface: A fashionable poem about a labourer is judged clumsily written.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue, 'line on worker' puts the line after the worker; the 'a' only smooths the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something inelegantly means doing it clumsily, lacking grace or polish.

clue.text: Doctor knocked back drink, once again dispatched everywhere

definitions.note: adverb clueing an adjective: present everywhere

indicators.note: knocking something back sends it the other way, so the doctor's letters are turned around

parts.note: a nip is a small drink of spirits

explanation.surface: A doctor downs a drink and then is sent off on another round of house calls.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Knocked back' looks like the drink being gulped, but it reverses the doctor.
explanation.definitionFit: Something omnipresent is present in all places at once, found absolutely all over.

clue.text: Confidence bound to be picked up

indicators.note: picking up a signal means hearing it, so the word is judged by its sound

explanation.surface: Someone's self-assurance is sure to be noticed.
explanation.definitionFit: Trust is faith or reliance placed in someone, the belief that they will not let you down.

clue.text: Clouds having been formed containing radioactive element, note

indicators.note: formed suggests the letters are shaped into something new
the reworked letters hold the next pieces inside them

parts.note: U is the symbol for uranium
the sixth note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: Clouds that have formed around a radioactive element, recorded in a note.
explanation.definitionFit: Nebulae are vast interstellar clouds of gas and dust seen in space.

clue.text: Novel with fantastic genre to flog in bulletin

explanation.surface: A news report about a fantasy novel being sold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel' and 'to flog' (to sell) look like book-trade talk, but give NEW and LASH (to whip).
explanation.definitionFit: A newsflash is a short urgent news item broadcast between programmes, a brief bulletin.

clue.text: Abnormal sort of water in Derwent's banks

indicators.note: the water brand is put inside the two edge letters
a river's banks are its two edges, so only the outer letters of the river name are kept

parts.note: first and last letters of the river name
a brand of bottled mineral water

explanation.surface: Something strange is found in the water between the banks of the Derwent, an English river.
explanation.definitionFit: Deviant behaviour departs from what is usual or accepted, so it is not normal.

clue.text: Send on deployment of troops, say, following Thirty Years War?

parts.note: to post a letter is to send it
troops formed up again, a re-formation

explanation.surface: An order to dispatch troops after a long European war.
explanation.walkthrough: The Thirty Years War (1618-48) came after the Protestant Reformation, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: The Post-Reformation era is the period after the Protestant split, when that religious war took place.

clue.text: Castigate attempt at humour, to a degree

explanation.surface: Mock a feeble joke to some extent.
explanation.definitionFit: To castigate is to reprimand severely, and to punish is to penalise for wrongdoing.

clue.text: Go off northwards after car, I hear

indicators.note: in a down entry, going north means reading upwards

parts.note: to rot is to go bad

explanation.surface: Someone reports a car breaking down on its way north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I hear' looks like a sound signal; it is the definition, a cryptic description of a listener.
explanation.definitionFit: Auditor comes from Latin for hearer, one who hears, which is what each 'I' who hears is.

clue.text: Used to give support, at first

indicators.note: this places the backing word at the front, ahead of the giving word

parts.note: to second a motion is to support it
to hand something over is to give it

explanation.surface: Something old was once employed to prop things up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Give support' looks like one phrase, but the two words are separate pieces with the second one put first.
explanation.definitionFit: Second-hand goods have already been owned and used by someone else before you.

clue.text: I'm not interested in female item of clothing

explanation.surface: Someone shrugs off a woman's fashion item.
explanation.definitionFit: So what? is a dismissive retort showing indifference to what has just been said.

clue.text: Depict resistance fighters on edge, retreating

indicators.note: retreating means going backwards, so the whole string is read from the end

explanation.surface: A portrait of resistance fighters backing away from a precipice.
explanation.definitionFit: To mirror something is to reflect or represent it faithfully, a way of portraying it.

clue.text: Maybe what could make inventor pour ale

indicators.note: the following words could be made into something else by reordering

explanation.surface: Asking what might lead an inventor to pour beer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Maybe what' looks like a question opener; it is the definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: In grammar 'what' can introduce a clause, as in 'take what you need', so it is an example.

clue.text: Condescend to listen to EU citizen

indicators.note: what we need is the word as heard, not as spelt

parts.note: to deign is to stoop to do something

explanation.surface: Someone stoops to hear out a fellow European.
explanation.definitionFit: A Dane is a person from Denmark, a member state of the European Union.

clue.text: Inclusive approach gets old man aboard Britain's new vessel

indicators.note: aboard means inside a vessel, so the old man goes in
new suggests a fresh arrangement of the letters

explanation.surface: An old sailor boards a new British ship with an inclusive approach.
explanation.definitionFit: Bipartisanship is cooperation between two political parties, an approach that brings both sides in.

clue.text: Children's writer's block has no end

indicators.note: with no end, the final letter is taken away

explanation.surface: An author's writer's block is endless.
explanation.walkthrough: J. M. Barrie wrote Peter Pan. 'Writer's block' is split: writer joins the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: J. M. Barrie is the Scottish author best known for Peter Pan, a story for young readers.

clue.text: Crazy whirl upstaging enchanting event?

indicators.note: crazy means wild and disordered, so the following letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A wild spinning dance steals the show at a magical gathering.
explanation.walkthrough: Walpurgis Night, the eve of 1 May, is when witches are said to gather; 'enchanting' puns on spellcasting.
explanation.definitionFit: Folklore holds that witches hold their sabbath on this night, a festival of spells.

clue.text: Throw up, at first, on new drug

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the preceding word is used

explanation.surface: Someone vomits at the first taste of a new drug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Throw up' reads as vomit; throw is the definition (as a horse throws a rider).
explanation.definitionFit: A bucking mount that dislodges its rider sends him or her to the ground, knocking the person out of the saddle.

clue.text: A lot of craft to satisfy a welcoming crowd

indicators.note: to welcome is to take in, so the crowd word goes inside

parts.note: a lot is a group or bunch

explanation.surface: Plenty of handiwork to please a gathering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A lot of craft' reads as lots of skill, but craft here means boats.
explanation.definitionFit: A flotilla is a fleet of small ships or boats sailing together, many vessels at once.

clue.text: Goddess, we're told, is like a carrier of blood

indicators.note: being told something means hearing it, so sound matters

explanation.surface: We hear that a goddess is a sort of blood carrier.
explanation.definitionFit: Venous means relating to veins, the vessels that carry blood back to the heart.

clue.text: Venomous man, a day tripper

explanation.surface: A spiteful fellow out on a day trip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Day tripper' looks like a holidaymaker; split it so day gives D and tripper is someone on LSD.
explanation.definitionFit: An acidhead is a habitual LSD user, someone who goes on hallucinogenic trips.

clue.text: One learner guided around in class is ignorant

indicators.note: the guiding word goes around the class phrase

parts.note: in form, as a school form is a class

explanation.surface: A student led around a classroom knows nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: A form is a school class in Britain, so in class is IN FORM.
explanation.definitionFit: Ill-informed people have poor or wrong knowledge, so they are badly lacking in facts.

clue.text: Hinder false advertiser, one offering advice

indicators.note: false means not genuine, so the next word's letters are rearranged

parts.note: hinder as an adjective means rear, as in hind legs

explanation.surface: Obstruct a dishonest advertiser who keeps giving tips.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hinder' reads as the verb to obstruct; it is the adjective (rhymes with 'finder') meaning rear.
explanation.definitionFit: A back-seat driver is a passenger who gives unwanted directions, an unwelcome adviser.

clue.text: Loveless letters penned by thick aristocrat

indicators.note: penned means shut in, so these go inside the thick word
love is zero in tennis, so without love the O goes

explanation.surface: A dim noblewoman writes letters without affection.
explanation.definitionFit: A viscountess is a noblewoman ranking between a countess and a baroness, a member of the peerage.

clue.text: Pragmatic criminal in court takes fellow in

indicators.note: criminal means crooked, so the letters are bent out of order
taking someone in means letting them inside

explanation.surface: A practical crook in court takes in another man.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone unromantic takes a practical, unsentimental view of things.

clue.text: Make unclear, short publicity text

indicators.note: short means cut off, so the last letter goes

parts.note: the promotional copy on a book jacket

explanation.surface: An instruction to make a brief advert vague.
explanation.definitionFit: To blur something is to make its outline indistinct or fuzzy, so it is hard to see.

clue.text: Heartless fool screening film in old age

indicators.note: screening means hiding behind, so the film goes inside
with its heart gone, the middle letter of the fool word is removed

explanation.surface: A silly person showing a movie at a care home.
explanation.definitionFit: Ninety is a great age to reach, an example of being very elderly.

clue.text: Admitting depression, crooks joining church recover

indicators.note: admitting means letting in, so the depression goes inside the crooks

parts.note: a valley, a dip in the land

explanation.surface: Depressed criminals find their way back to health by going to church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Depression' reads as low mood, but it is a dip in the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: To convalesce is to regain health and strength gradually after an illness.

clue.text: Echo behind cattle car

indicators.note: behind places the first piece after the second

parts.note: a French breed of beef cattle

explanation.surface: A sound comes from behind a herd and a car.
explanation.definitionFit: A limousine is a large luxurious car, often driven by a chauffeur.

clue.text: Kind of leaves a prison in this way

explanation.surface: Someone escapes from jail this way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaves' reads as a verb (departs); it is the noun, foliage.
explanation.definitionFit: Acanthus is a plant whose deeply cut foliage is copied in Corinthian columns.

clue.text: Responding with original, moving chapter

indicators.note: shifting the chapter letter elsewhere changes the order

explanation.surface: Reacting to a novel, emotive chapter.
explanation.walkthrough: C (chapter) moves from the front to the fourth place.
explanation.definitionFit: Reactive means acting in response to something rather than taking the initiative.

clue.text: Subject promises to settle coastal area, being quarrelsome

parts.note: the content of a book is its subject matter
IOUs are written promises to pay debts
a ness is a headland, as in Dungeness

explanation.surface: Debts and land disputes on the coast cause arguments.
explanation.definitionFit: Contentiousness is a tendency to provoke arguments, the state of being argumentative.

clue.text: Not dressed in rubbish fabric

indicators.note: the undressed word goes within the rubbish word

explanation.surface: Someone is naked in shabby cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: Tabaret is a striped upholstery fabric of silk with alternating satin stripes.

clue.text: Vain Englishman and American crossing river

indicators.note: the two nationals sit on either side of the river, as if across it

parts.note: Australian slang for an English person

explanation.surface: A conceited Englishman and an American cross a river together.
explanation.definitionFit: A pompous person is self-important and conceited, full of his or her own dignity.

clue.text: Two versions of small figure to placate

parts.note: S as the abbreviation and WEE as the Scottish word

explanation.surface: Two kinds of small statue are offered to calm someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To sweeten someone is to make them more agreeable, as by a gift that mollifies.

clue.text: Mobile phone with charm and a reluctance to innovate?

indicators.note: mobile means able to move, so the letters of the next word shift around

parts.note: obi, or obeah, is a West Indian charm or fetish

explanation.surface: Someone shuns the latest mobile despite its appeal.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a loose definition: neophobia is fear of anything new.
explanation.definitionFit: Neophobia is a dread of novelty, which makes a person unwilling to try fresh ideas.

clue.text: Eats meal briefly, in rush

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: to have a meal is to eat it

explanation.surface: Someone bolts a hurried snack.
explanation.definitionFit: Haste is hurry or excessive speed, so a rush.

clue.text: Agreement to embrace John? Nothing is impossible

indicators.note: embracing means holding within, so the agreement word wraps around John

parts.note: both john and can are US slang for a toilet

explanation.surface: A deal involving John looks impossible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nothing is impossible' reads as a motto, but Nothing is wordplay and 'impossible' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: No can do is a colloquial refusal saying something cannot be done at all.

clue.text: Regularly in toupee? You must be joking

indicators.note: regularly means at fixed intervals, so every other letter is taken

explanation.surface: Someone laughs at the idea of wearing a hairpiece.
explanation.definitionFit: Nope is a casual refusal, an informal no, as is the exclamation of disbelief.

clue.text: Crustacean luckily protecting back bones

indicators.note: back tells us to read the concealed letters in the opposite direction
the words shield the answer inside them

parts.note: the letters across the join of the two words

explanation.surface: A lucky crab's shell guards its spine.
explanation.definitionFit: The ulna is a forearm bone; ulnae is its plural, the inner bones of both arms.

clue.text: It's almost the end in sentence

explanation.surface: A grammar remark that the full stop is nearly reached.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sentence' reads as grammar, but it is a jail term.
explanation.definitionFit: The home stretch is the final section of a race or task, close to finishing.

clue.text: The writer's to offer books without forethought

explanation.surface: An author decides to donate books rashly.
explanation.definitionFit: Improvident people fail to plan or save for the future, lacking prudent foresight.

clue.text: Singular art including most blue

parts.note: archaic 'thou addest': art signals the old second-person form

explanation.surface: A peculiar artwork includes the bluest of colours.
explanation.walkthrough: Art is the archaic 'thou art', so 'art including' becomes the old second-person verb for adding, thou addest.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling blue means feeling sad, so the most blue is the most unhappy.

clue.text: Person managing to seize one unoriginal type

indicators.note: seizing means grabbing hold, so the numeral goes inside

explanation.surface: A manager grabs someone lacking ideas.
explanation.definitionFit: A copier imitates others' work rather than creating anything new, a plagiarist.

clue.text: Kid by cool water experiencing heat

indicators.note: by means beside, so the child word sits next to the rest

explanation.surface: A child by the cold sea on a hot day.
explanation.definitionFit: A female animal in season is on heat, ready to mate.
